claims.text: Schwab's RIA custody strategy is built around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, and around deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody to add value for RIAs.
Schwab states the RIA custody business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service and breadth to support advisers as their businesses and clients' needs become more complex.
Schwab believes it can maintain its competitive position primarily through its sales, support, technology and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete and succeed.
Schwab aims to be the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products and technology in addition to custody and service.
Schwab describes its offering as a differentiated, full-service platform built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody, operational excellence, and dedicated service and support.
In advisor services, Schwab is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

Trade press reports Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million in AUM, positioning its role as providing a platform and support ecosystem.

Trade press reports Schwab wants to give RIAs equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing and long-short strategies, positioning itself as the RIA's bank.
Schwab's strategic priorities include broadening support for RIAs while improving monetization.

Schwab states it maintains its competitive position in Advisor Services through sales, support, technology and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete and succeed, with superior service and technology providing a scalable platform.

Schwab states it is deepening relationships with RIA firms by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody, including grown lending support, alternatives capability and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.

Schwab states its priority is to provide the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, with wealth tools, investment/lending products and technology in addition to custody and service.
Schwab states that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while helping new advisors transition to independence.

Schwab states focus areas for its custody offerings include pledged-asset lending, private-market investing and long-short strategies, and playing the role of being RIAs' bank to help manage both sides of clients' balance sheets.
Schwab states it will continue to focus on custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, providing a platform and support ecosystem to help advisors support clients and thrive.
Schwab states the opportunity going forward in advisor services is to offer a more curated set of alternatives to advisors rather than primarily just custodying the assets.

Schwab states it has rounded out its offering to advisors by adding more lending capabilities, including a structured asset lending program enabling clients to borrow against alternative and restricted or private shares.

Schwab states that, as the largest custodian for advisors, it is focused on creating long-term value and access and on investing in innovation, capabilities and service to help advisors grow and investors succeed.
